Spill-over runs in order and cascades, with cell 6 going to LOST: "Do not compute the six violations simultaneously" and "for component 6, add v to s instead". The mode check uses >=U and <=D, keeps the mode in between, and allows one change per period: "at least u_i", "at most d_i", "a component with d_i < x_i < u_i keeps whichever flag it already has", "A flag changes at most once per iteration". Release uses floor /4 or /2 from a snapshot applied all at once, sends ELEVATED upstream and cell 1 to LOST, and does not enforce capacity: "Compute all six amounts before changing any value", "ACTIVE component 1: t_1 is added to s", "never corrected if it arises in iteration 5". The reset uses a strict >G and floor halving into LOST: "strictly more than B (that is, more than 38)". The document adds "Nothing else changes x, the flags, or s at any time" and "Every amount that leaves the state vector is added to s". Both are consistent with the abstract process and add nothing to it. All data tables match.

domainPull: The pull was strongest at \"Gauss-Seidel projection sweep\". A real projection onto a box throws the excess away, but here it is carried into component i+1. The \"active-set flag\" is the second strong point: in real optimisation a constraint is active when it binds at the bound c_i, but here the flag turns on at a separate threshold u_i that can sit below c_i and turns off only at d_i (hysteresis). Lesser pulls are \"penalty step\", which halves the state rather than adding a cost term, and \"slack\", which is a running loss tally rather than a gap variable.
